headline: Labor and the Greens seal a deal on capital gains tax and negative gearing — the biggest property investment shake-up in years — while GXAI.AX took the portfolio's biggest hit today, dropping 3.2%.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: Worst mover in the portfolio today. The AI ETF was dragged down by Google-related names — two of Google's top DeepMind and Gemini researchers publicly defected to rivals OpenAI and Anthropic last night, rattling confidence in Google's AI leadership. Since GXAI holds a big chunk of Google/Alphabet, that news hit the ETF hard on the ASX today.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: A soft day for emerging markets, mostly driven by the Aussie dollar falling sharply (down 1.1% vs the USD). When the AUD drops, it can affect how Aussie-listed ETFs track foreign assets. No major single country news — just broad risk-off sentiment flowing through to emerging market equities.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Pilbara slipped another 1.1% today, continuing a rough run — the position is now down nearly 19% overall. Lithium prices remain soft and the market is still sceptical about when demand will truly pick up. Analyst commentary floating around today is divided: some see a 'comeback' forming, others think another reset is possible before recovery.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: A quiet dip of 0.5% today, mostly reflecting the broader global market mood — last night's US session saw the S&P 500 and NASDAQ both fall, and that flows through into VDHG's international holdings when it opens on the ASX.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: Down about 0.5% today, tracking last night's US market weakness where the NASDAQ fell 1.4%. No specific news on this ETF — it's just reflecting the drag from US tech stocks pulling back across the board.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy ETF
movers.note: Essentially flat today, holding up better than you'd expect given crude oil (WTI) dropped 2.4% last night to $73. The ETF may have lagged the oil move slightly — watch this one over the next couple of sessions as cheaper oil typically flows through to energy company earnings expectations.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two had a solid night last session, up 1.8%. The GTA 6 hype machine is still running hot — pre-order information for PS5 and Xbox editions is now widely circulating, keeping investor excitement elevated around the release. The stock is now up 6.4% overall from your cost base.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft bounced 1.5% last session, helped by a couple of positive catalysts: the company announced a major 20-year power deal with Chevron to fuel its West Texas AI data centre, and Satya Nadella has been making headlines with bullish comments about Microsoft's AI momentum. The stock is still down about 16% from your buy price, but the narrative is improving.

movers.name: Alphabet (Google)
movers.note: Google slipped 0.6% last session after news broke that two senior researchers — one from DeepMind and one from the Gemini team — jumped ship to OpenAI and Anthropic respectively. Markets worry about brain drain at Google's AI division. The CEO has been talking up AI's impact on revenue, but losing key talent to rivals is a real concern for investors.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX — biggest portfolio drop today, -3.21%
watch_today.detail: The AI ETF fell hard today off the back of Google researcher defections to OpenAI and Anthropic hitting sentiment on AI/tech names. It's now down 5.8% overall. The news risk around Google hasn't fully settled — hold for now and watch whether sentiment stabilises over the next few sessions before adding.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX — down 19% overall, lithium still hurting
watch_today.detail: Pilbara dropped another 1.1% today and is sitting on an -18.8% loss on your position. Fastmarkets are calling a 'new phase' for lithium where demand eventually outpaces supply, but that's a medium-term story. Right now, price is still weak and there's no clear catalyst to turn it around. Hold unless you want to reassess your risk tolerance.

watch_today.title: Labor–Greens CGT and negative gearing deal confirmed today
watch_today.detail: Big political news today: Labor has done a deal with the Greens to pass changes to capital gains tax (CGT — the tax you pay when you sell an asset at a profit) and negative gearing (where property investors claim rental losses against their income). The 50% CGT discount on investments held over 12 months is set to be reduced, and negative gearing on existing properties will be tightened. If you hold property investments or are planning to sell investments, this is worth watching closely. The exact start date has also been confirmed — check the news.com.au story for details.

watch_today.title: GOOG — brain drain risk, keep an eye on it
watch_today.detail: Two of Google's top AI researchers (from DeepMind and the Gemini team) have left for OpenAI and Anthropic. Markets reacted with a 0.55% dip last session. The CEO says AI has 'completely changed the revenue picture', which is positive, but losing key scientists to rivals is a slow-burn risk. Your position is up 12.8% overall — hold, but monitor for further departures.

watch_today.title: MSFT — Chevron power deal and AI momentum building
watch_today.detail: Microsoft locked in a 20-year power agreement with Chevron for its West Texas AI data centre — a sign the company is seriously scaling up its AI infrastructure. Stock rose 1.5% last session. Still down 16% from your cost base, but the trend is improving. Hold and watch next earnings.

watch_today.title: Crude oil dropped 2.4% last night — watch FUEL.AX this week
watch_today.detail: WTI crude oil fell from $74.82 to $73 last night. FUEL.AX barely moved today (up 0.1%), but cheaper oil usually hits energy company profit forecasts within a few days. If oil stays soft, expect FUEL.AX to feel more pressure later this week.

markets.summary: Last night's US session was a rough one — both the S&P 500 and NASDAQ sold off, with tech leading the decline. Google researcher defections to OpenAI and Anthropic spooked AI-sector investors, and oil dropped over 2%. The Aussie dollar also fell 1.1% against the USD, sitting at 69.2 cents. ASX 200 data wasn't available at close today.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Down 0.9% last night — broad US market weakness, tech dragged it lower.

indicators.name: NASDAQ
indicators.note: Down 1.4% last night, hit hardest by AI/tech names including Google falling on researcher departures.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: Aussie dollar fell to 69.2 US cents today. Traders are reassessing RBA rate hike expectations despite some bets still lingering.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Oil dropped 2.4% last night to $73 — pressure on energy stocks and FUEL.AX going forward.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Slight dip but gold remains elevated — still well above $4,000 as a safe-haven asset.

politics.summary: The big story today is Labor and the Greens sealing a deal on capital gains tax and negative gearing reform — the most significant change to property investment tax rules in decades. There's also ongoing noise about RBA rate decisions and what US rate moves mean for Australians.

stories.title: Labor and Greens confirm deal on CGT and negative gearing reforms
stories.why_it_matters: Labor has struck a deal with the Greens to pass changes to capital gains tax (CGT) — the tax on profits from selling investments — and negative gearing, which lets property investors deduct rental losses from their taxable income. The 50% CGT discount that investors have enjoyed on assets held over 12 months is set to be wound back, and negative gearing on existing investment properties will be restricted. This is a major shift for anyone who owns investment property or holds assets they plan to sell. Property investors are the hardest hit. The end date for the existing $33 billion tax perk has now been officially confirmed — check the news.com.au story for the specific date.

stories.title: $33bn tax perk's end date finally confirmed
stories.why_it_matters: The $33 billion tax concession tied to CGT discounts and negative gearing now has an official end date confirmed. This gives property investors a clear deadline to plan around. If you own investment properties or are thinking about buying one, this is directly relevant to your financial strategy. Anyone relying on these perks to make investment properties cash-flow-positive will need to rethink their numbers.

stories.title: New superannuation ban to come for millions of Australians as part of tax changes
stories.why_it_matters: Buried in the broader tax reform package is a new restriction on superannuation — millions of Australians will be affected by what appears to be a ban on certain super-related strategies as part of the Labor-Greens deal. Full details are still emerging, but if you have self-managed super or use super as part of a tax strategy, this is worth reading carefully.

stories.title: Major banks split after RBA interest rate warning
stories.why_it_matters: Australia's big banks are now openly disagreeing about whether the RBA (Reserve Bank of Australia) will raise interest rates further. Some are saying the RBA's recent warning signals more hikes are coming, while others think the central bank is close to done. This split matters for mortgage holders and anyone with variable-rate debt — it also explains why the Aussie dollar has been volatile today, sitting around 69.2 US cents.

ai.summary: The dominant AI story today is Google losing senior researchers to OpenAI and Anthropic, which hit GOOG's share price and dragged GXAI.AX down on the ASX. Microsoft is countering with bullish AI infrastructure news. South Australia is also pushing hard to attract AI data centres.

stories.title: Google loses top DeepMind and Gemini researchers to OpenAI and Anthropic
stories.source: Search Engine Journal / Investor's Business Daily
stories.why_it_matters: Two high-profile AI scientists have left Google — one from DeepMind (Google's flagship AI research lab) and one from the Gemini team (Google's main AI model) — to join OpenAI and Anthropic respectively. This is the kind of brain drain that genuinely worries investors: these aren't junior staff, they're the people who built the technology. Google's stock dipped 0.55% last session on the news. For GXAI.AX holders, this contributed directly to today's 3.2% drop since the ETF has heavy exposure to Alphabet.

stories.title: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella: 'You can't stop us on AI'
stories.why_it_matters: Satya Nadella made headlines with an unusually direct challenge to every AI company — basically saying Microsoft has the infrastructure, the partnerships, and the talent to outlast the competition. The company backed this up with a concrete 20-year power deal with Chevron for its AI data centre in West Texas. This kind of long-term energy infrastructure commitment signals Microsoft is treating AI as a permanent, capital-intensive business — not a passing trend. Good signal for MSFT holders.

stories.title: Google DeepMind and A24 announce first AI-film research partnership
stories.why_it_matters: Google's DeepMind division has teamed up with A24 — the indie film studio behind Everything Everywhere All at Once and Midsommar — in what's described as a first-of-its-kind research partnership. The idea is to explore how AI can be used in creative filmmaking. It's an interesting play by Google to show AI has practical creative uses beyond chatbots and search, potentially helping rehabilitate the brand narrative after the researcher departures story.

stories.title: SA pushes for AI data centres as industry says it's not asking for subsidies
stories.why_it_matters: South Australia is actively courting AI companies to build data centres in the state, and the tech industry is saying it doesn't need government subsidies — just the right regulatory environment and reliable energy access. For Australian investors in AI-exposed funds like GXAI.AX, domestic AI infrastructure growth is a slow-burn positive. It also signals that AI's electricity demand is becoming a real policy conversation in Australia.

sport.summary: NRL Round 17 kicks off Thursday with Eels vs Rabbitohs. The big injury news is Latrell Mitchell — his injury is worse than first thought. Nathan Cayless has left Parramatta to chase a head coaching role. In AFL, there's coaching instability at two big clubs and Serena Williams is back for Wimbledon.

stories.title: Latrell Mitchell injury worse than first feared — major blow for premiership contender
stories.why_it_matters: Latrell Mitchell's injury has been upgraded to more serious than initially reported — a significant blow for his club's premiership ambitions. The full extent and timeline aren't confirmed in the available details, but 'worse than first feared' is never a good sign heading into the back half of the season. Worth keeping an eye on official club injury updates ahead of Round 17.

stories.title: Nathan Cayless departs Parramatta Eels to pursue head coaching opportunity
stories.why_it_matters: Nathan Cayless, who has been a key part of Parramatta's coaching staff, has officially left the Eels to pursue a head coaching role elsewhere. This is a significant behind-the-scenes move for the Eels, who play in Round 17 this Thursday against the Rabbitohs at CommBank Stadium. Coaching staff continuity matters during a season push.

stories.title: 2026 NRL Signings Tracker: Hunt to play on with Broncos; Geyer joins Bears
stories.why_it_matters: The NRL transfer market is heating up with the June 30 deadline approaching. Ben Hunt has confirmed he'll play on with the Broncos, and Jake Geyer has signed with the Bears. Several more big-name moves are expected before the end of the month — keep an eye on the Zero Tackle story on five players likely to find new clubs before June 30.

stories.title: AFL coaching instability: Two coaches, two big clubs, two very different problems
stories.why_it_matters: Two AFL clubs are dealing with significant coaching headaches right now, according to analysis from AFL.com.au. One senior coach has been described as 'gettable' — meaning clubs can approach them — while another club has a worrying injury report on a key Cat player who missed their last game. The AFL is at the pointy end of the season where stability in the coaching box really counts.

stories.title: Serena Williams earns Wimbledon singles wild card for comeback
stories.why_it_matters: Serena Williams has been granted a wild card entry into Wimbledon singles — continuing her comeback to professional tennis. At 44, this is a remarkable story. Wimbledon wild cards are handed out at the discretion of the All England Club to players of note, and Serena's inclusion will generate enormous global attention for the tournament.
